prompt: In the textbook page-I/O model, table R has 2,000 pages and table S has 400 pages. Neither has an index on the join column. The join has 52 buffer pages, so a block nested loop can hold 50 pages of the outer table at a time. Which plan reads the fewest pages, and why?

options.text: R on the outer side, because the larger table should be read only once
options.explanation: R is then read once, but its 2,000 pages make 40 blocks, so S is rescanned 40 times. What matters is how many times the inner table is reread, not reading the big table once.

options.text: S on the outer side, because its 400 pages make only 8 blocks, so R is rescanned just 8 times
options.explanation: Correct. The inner table is reread once per outer block. S splits into 8 blocks of 50 pages, against 40 blocks for R, so the smaller table belongs outside: about 16,400 page I/Os against 18,000.

options.text: It makes no difference which table is outside, because both are read in full
options.explanation: Both orientations read every page at least once, but the number of inner rescans differs: 8 with S outside and 40 with R outside.

options.text: S on the outer side, read one page at a time to leave memory free
options.explanation: Using one outer page per block means 400 blocks and 400 full scans of R, roughly 800,000 page I/Os. Bigger blocks are the whole point of a block nested loop.

workedExample:
A block nested loop reads the outer table once, in blocks, and scans the whole inner table once per block. So count the blocks for each orientation:

1. R outside: 2,000 pages in blocks of 50 makes 40 blocks, so the 400-page S is scanned 40 times. About 2,000 + 16,000 = 18,000 page I/Os.
2. S outside: 400 pages in blocks of 50 makes 8 blocks, so the 2,000-page R is scanned 8 times. About 400 + 16,000 = 16,400 page I/Os.
3. One outer page per block throws away the benefit: 400 scans of R.

The smaller table goes outside here because it produces fewer blocks. When the two sizes are close, rounding up the last part-full block can change the answer, so compare both orientations. More buffer pages would shrink the block count further.
